title: Korean Proverbs (속담 & 사자성어)
description: Classic Korean proverbs and traditional expressions with English meanings

items.translation: A piece of cake (lit. eating cold porridge).
Every little bit counts (lit. gathering dust makes a mountain).

items.target: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다.
items.translation: Speak kindly to receive kind words (What goes around comes around).
Joy comes after hardship (No pain, no gain).
Starting is half the battle (Well begun is half done).
Look before you leap (lit. tap even a stone bridge before crossing).

items.target: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다.
items.translation: Birds hear daytime talk, and mice hear nighttime talk (Walls have ears).

items.target: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다.
items.translation: Speak kindly to receive kind words (Treat others as you wish to be treated).
All show and no substance (lit. hollow puffed-rice snack).
Joy comes at the end of hardship (No pain, no gain).
Many a little makes a mickle (lit. gathering dust creates a great mountain).
A frog in a well (A person of narrow vision / sheltered and unaware).
Even monkeys fall from trees (Even experts make mistakes).
Two heads are better than one (lit. even a sheet of paper is lighter when lifted together).
Eating comes first (lit. even Mount Geumgang is best viewed after eating).
Locking the stable after the horse has bolted (lit. fixing the barn after losing the cow).
Hard work never goes to waste (lit. will a tower built with care collapse?).
He who steals a needle will steal an ox (Minor misdeeds lead to major crimes).
Better safe than sorry / always double-check (lit. ask directions even on a familiar road).
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Harming someone then pretending to help (lit. giving a disease, then offering medicine).
A piece of cake (lit. eating rice cake while lying down).
As easy as pie (lit. eating cooled porridge).
Effortlessly easy (lit. swimming while touching the ground).
Pie in the sky / an unattainable desire (lit. a rice cake in a painting).
A drop in the bucket (lit. blood on a bird's foot).
It is darkest under the lamp (Overlooking what is right under one's nose).
Speak of the devil (lit. speak of the tiger and it comes).

items.target: 개구리 올챙이 적 생각 못 한다.
items.translation: The frog forgets its tadpole days (Becoming arrogant after achieving success).
A guilty conscience needs no accuser (lit. the thief's own foot tingles with guilt).

items.target: 뛰는 놈 위에 나는 놈 있다.
items.translation: There is always someone better (lit. above a runner, there is a flier).
Old habits die hard (lit. habits formed at age three last until age eighty).

items.target: 발 없는 말이 천 리 간다.
items.translation: Rumors spread fast (lit. words without feet travel a thousand miles).
Killing two birds with one stone (一石二鳥)
East question, west answer; giving an irrelevant reply (東問西答)
A resolution lasting only three days; short-lived resolve (作心三日)
Great talents mature over time; late bloomer (大器晩成)
Ten spoons make one bowl of rice; many small contributions make a big difference (十匙一飯)
Preparedness prevents disaster; where there is precaution, there is no worry (有備無患)
Putting yourself in someone else's shoes; mutual empathy (易地思之)
Justice will ultimately prevail; all things return to the rightful state (事必歸正)
Blue comes from indigo; the pupil surpasses the master (靑出於藍)
Sweetness comes after bitterness; joy succeeds hardship (苦盡甘來)
Fall seven times, stand up eight; indomitable perseverance (七顚八起)
Reap what you sow; suffering the natural consequences of one's own deeds (自業自得)
Repaying a kindness even beyond death (結草報恩)
Deep contemplation and careful deliberation (深思熟考)
One bad fish muddies the entire stream; one bad apple spoils the bunch (一魚濁水)
Excess is as bad as deficiency; moderation is key (過猶不及)
Sharing joys and sorrows together; enduring hardships and pleasures as one (同苦同樂)
